//: The edge's SECURITY POLICY, and its own file for the same reason gateway-routes.json is:
so it can be reviewed and diffed on its own, and so it travels with the gateway wherever the
gateway is hosted.
Δ C127 — it was a `Gateway` section of appsettings.json, and that is where finding 02 came
from. The lightweight replica co-locates the edge and the 22 domain services in ONE process
(AppServices, C125), whose `DropCoLocatedAppSettings` target removes every referenced
project's appsettings.json — one content root cannot hold twenty-three files of that name.
So on every replica deployment the whole section was absent and the CODE DEFAULTS applied:
· Attestation:SensitiveOperations fell back to [] — D-30 marked NOTHING sensitive, so
Mode=Enforce would have enforced attestation on zero operations, silently.
· RateLimits:Policies fell back to {} — all 70 routes logged 'policy not configured;
applying no limit', so the edge had no rate limit at all (ADD §12.6 geo scraping,
trip-share abuse, the auth and sos buckets).
· BlockedPathPrefixes fell back to its compiled ['/v1/internal'].
Nothing in any test noticed, because every in-process suite composes the gateway from THIS
directory, where the file was present.
GatewayApplication.Build loads it explicitly and ApiGateway.csproj pins it to the output
directory, which is what makes it survive into the co-located image — the same two lines
gateway-routes.json has always had.

//BlockedPathPrefixes: D3' §0 puts the service-to-service plane on mesh mTLS, and the prefix convention for it is
/v1/internal. Three routes are service-to-service and are NOT under that prefix, so before
C127 the edge routed all three to the public internet under an ordinary per-service rule:
· POST /v1/fare/calculate       — prices a completed ride (`fare` route, Order 50)
· GET  /v1/content/templates/*  — notification-svc's D-26 render path (`content`, Order 50)
Each fails closed on its own shared-secret filter, so this is defence in depth rather than a
hole being closed — except for the template render, whose filter degrades to *open* when
Content:InternalApiKey is unset, which is a deliberate availability trade argued in that
service. Every caller of all three uses a direct service address (Fare__RideBaseUrl,
Notification__ContentBaseUrl, Ride__IamBaseUrl), never the gateway, so refusing them at the
edge costs nothing. C042 replaces the whole arrangement with a SPIFFE peer identity.
Matching is StartsWithSegments, so /v1/users/lookup does not block /v1/users/me.

ForwardedHeaders.//: C009 / C125 must add the HAProxy address here, or every caller shares one rate-limit bucket.

//: D-31. MinimumVersion is the hard floor: below it every proxied request is answered 426.
RecommendedVersion is the soft floor: at or above the hard floor but below this,
GET /v1/version/check reports updateRequired with isMandatory:false so the app can show a
dismissible prompt (US-17.1 soft vs US-17.2 mandatory).
The values below are placeholders for the first store builds; Wave 4a/4b set the real ones.
D-30. SensitiveOperations is exactly the set of operations carrying the X-Attestation
parameter in backend/contracts/*.yaml — auth, payments, ride accept, wallet and SOS
(D3' §0). ApiGateway.Tests asserts the two sets are equal, so an endpoint that becomes
sensitive in the contract fails the build until it is listed here.
Coarse edge ceilings per route and caller address (D6' §8.2). The named business limits
stay in the services that own them — OTP 5/h + 60 s cooldown (D-32) keys on a phone number
and proxy location requests 5/h + 30/d (P-12) key on a booker id, neither of which the
edge can see. Capacity is the burst; RefillTokens per RefillPeriod is the sustained rate.
